title: Chapter 881
paragraphs: Chapter 881
Episode 220. Unwearied (3)
'Could it be... Is Jikelro falling behind?'
'If Jikelro loses, we must capture the labyrinth master of Hidden Palace!'
Despite pressuring Syris, the generals couldn't shake off their unease.

Originally, they wanted and expected to quickly deal with Syris and then support Jikelro. However, they could feel Jikelro's energy waning from behind, and Syris, who they thought they could capture soon, was still surviving.
"Even if you find me laughable, would it be okay to be so concerned about the battlefield of the first flagbearers?"
Thump-!
Syris swung his Ice Sword with wide eyes. Despite his body feeling heavy due to significant blood loss, it just meant he could radiate a stronger chill. The enemies were slowing down accordingly.
A pure white cold energy spread in all directions, filling the battlefield. Vilargul and Sikan swung their swords, discharging their magic to push back the cold.
Every time the Ice Sword and the two other swords clashed, the scattered cold and magic revealed the figures of the three momentarily.

In the generals' eyes, Syris, who was charging recklessly, definitely had a vulnerability. However, whenever they targeted this and stabbed their swords, they were counterattacked. The generals had a hard time understanding this throughout the fight.
"He's somehow holding on with the power of his weapon... But this level of chill is common underground. This will be the last time he withstands with just resilience!"
Vilargul grumbled, grinding his teeth.
He, like Jikelro, was a member of Lamierga, which meant he was a demon ruling the chloride region. He might not be on par with Jikelro, but he could use the chloride of the underworld.
Rumble-!
Suddenly, a huge pillar of fire rose in front of Syris. Syris, who was charging, had to dodge, and in the meantime, Sikan's sword grazed her side.

Syris had to pull herself out again, but there was already a new fire pillar in the rear. Regardless, Syris had to forcefully gather the power of the Ice Sword once more, using the cold to counteract the chloride.
"Huff, gasp...!"
The relentless assault of two swords and fire, along with the magic that suffocates her with every breath.

In this, Syris was barely hanging onto her life every moment. If she let her guard down for even a second, she would have suffered a fatal wound, and the same would have been true if she responded incorrectly.
Countless possibilities where life could be lost at any moment, and senses heightened to the limit within them.
Breaking through all of this and moving forward.
The truth is, fighting is always like that.
'How long has it been since such a fight.'

Looking back, Syris couldn't recall any recent instances of such 'inevitable' fights. Among those known as the representative second generation of each faction – Jin, Veradin, Dante, Syris – she had certainly been having easier battles than them.

She was born as the only daughter of Talaris, destined to inherit everything in Hidden Palace, always protected by Talaris and the Seven Swords of Hidden Palace, and even when alone facing a stronger opponent, she always had the special authority of Manbing.
And the two biggest wars of the past few years.
During the Sword Emperor War and the Demon War, Syris did participate, but she was in a better position than her peers.

Dante had been defending the Sword Emperor's Castle on his own before Gliek awoke, and Jin had culminated all the forces of the surface world to put an end to the Demon War. Veradin, although corrupted by Kelliark's scheme, ultimately overcame him and became a world ruler, dominating one axis of the world.
Of course, Syris knew well.
The reason she couldn't be the protagonist of a grand battle like them was not just because she was inferior to them.
For example, Syris has had no choice but to walk a relatively smooth path until now.

Thus, despite training harder than anyone, her actual battle experience where her life was in danger was inevitably lacking. Hidden Palace was always neutral until it became the Vamel Alliance, so they couldn't just barge into other factions intending to fight.
'Looking back, at the banquet... was the first time when I nearly died dueling Jin at the Runcandel Banquet.'

The memory of that day suddenly came up while the generals' swords were continuously blurring her sight. Entranced by that embarrassing but not unpleasant memory, Syris unconsciously deflected the enemies' swords.
Now, she is in a situation a hundred times more dangerous than that day.
But Syris was just beginning to feel the shell of her 'safe destiny' that had been binding her all this time breaking.
'As the master of Hidden Palace, I... should always be at the forefront when the world is in danger.'
World protection, the true meaning of Hidden Palace's existence that is not known to the world.
Now that the underground world has started invading the surface world, she had to step off the safe and smooth ground and walk on a thorny path.
Pit-!
Sikan's sword grazed Syris's neck.
A single battle, death danger renewed every second. Every time she overcame that danger, Syris was captivated by the sense of a clearer sight.
Little by little, she began to understand the meaning of 'growth' that Luna mentioned. Growth was about breaking through a new phase of fate. It was about standing up, overcoming fear and despair.
"These bastards are damn scary."
Syris spat out an expletive as she gripped Manbing.
Experience.
Instead of the lack of real-life fights, instead of having an easier fate, all the training she had done to not be underestimated, to erase her sense of inferiority.
Those occasional strong enemies she fought, the days when she was overwhelmed chasing after her friends who were always far ahead.
Syris realized that everything within him was writhing as if to explode. The triggers of death and fear were bursting the dam of experience that Syris had built up.
"Die already!"
The flame of Vilargul and the sword of Sikan attacked Syris again. The flame was offset by the cold, but his left shoulder was pierced by the sword.

Just as Sikan was about to explode the magic wrapped around his blade by twisting his sword, Syris screamed and swung his ice sword. With a wet thud, Sikan's arm was cut off, creating distance between the two.
Syris then pulled out Sikan's remaining arm and sword that had penetrated his shoulder and froze them with his ice sword.
"Haak, kheuk......!"
After crushing the frozen arm of Sikan underfoot, Syris also froze his shoulder to prevent the spread of magic.
'There's only one chance now.'
Even losing an arm and a sword, Sikan wouldn't lose enough combat power to be unable to fight. Moreover, Vilargul's flame was becoming fiercer.
Third Form of the Ice Sword, Avalanche.

As Syris unfolded the first form, the cold air scattered in the flame gathered into an ice sword. The large ice crystals pouring from the ice sword continuously created a deafening noise, and the warlords retreated momentarily from its power.
'Is this finally the last desperate struggle!'
It was right after inflicting a fatal wound through the shoulder. Unfolding such a large technique in the midst of this, it had to be his final move.
Though threatening, all they had to do was wait a few seconds for the explosion to dissipate. Then, Syris wouldn't have any power to fight.
Now, the warlords had only one concern left. If Jikalro finished off his opponent and Luna joined them, there would be no answer.
And then, in the moment they briefly checked the rear battlefield.
'Lord Jikalro!'
The warlords had to gulp down their breaths as they saw the scarlet energy that was coloring the entire sky. The endless spreading red sword energy signified Jikalro's death.

They had only encountered the red energy through the video distributed by Sakiel and the memories of the dead demons. They had been explained about its danger several times, but the red energy they saw firsthand far surpassed their imagination.
'It feels like my whole body is being torn apart just by looking at it...!'
'Excluding Lord Zito in the demon world, are there any demons... capable of handling that?'
The moment they had that thought, they were startled to see Luna striding towards them.
Moreover, she didn't look very tired.
"No way, already......!"
However, Luna waved dismissively at the flustered warlords, as if telling them there was nothing to fear.
"Ah, I have no intention of interfering, so continue what you were doing."
"……What?"
"Go and kill the Labyrinth Master. If you make me explain one more time, I'll just jump in and get rid of both of you. I promise, on the honor of Runcandel."
What could be the intention behind this?
The warlords couldn't understand, but they had no other choice. If they tried to flee, they would be immediately caught and killed by Luna.
Eventually, the warlords turned back towards Syris. It was after seeing Luna sit down and start eating some snacks.
"Give it your all."
The momentum of the Avalanche was quickly subsiding. In the gradually receding cold air, Syris was trembling, spitting up blood.
If Luna truly kept her promise, it would be time to finally cut off his tenacious life.

Without hesitation, the warlords started to charge at Syris, amplifying their magic to the maximum. Cutting off her neck, without a trace of aura or cold air left, would be easier than crushing a bug.
'Wait, no aura or cold air left at all?'
The first to sense that something was amiss was Vilargul.
No matter how tired, it would be normal to feel at least a bit of aura and cold air. Sikan also felt the same uneasiness after leaving about ten steps distance from Syris.
But it was already too late.
Fifth Form of the Ice Sword, Whiteout.
As Syris fell forward, he thrust the ice sword into the ground.
She used the Avalanche as a feint to unfold this. In the meantime, she had concentrated all the remaining aura and cold air to unfold the Fifth Form, Whiteout.
Compared to what Talaris unfolded in the past in Sword Emperor Castle, Syris' Whiteout was much smaller in scale.
As she had unfolded it with little remaining energy, it couldn't be otherwise, but it was enough to spread the same power as back then within ten steps.
Krrrrrr…!

Between Syris and the warlords, an absurdly sharp and solid ice flower surged. The shattered ice flower instantly pierced through the warlords' bodies, tearing them apart. Vilargul and Sikan had to be buried in the ice flower of Whiteout without even being able to scream.
However, Syris was unable to witness them being crushed and meeting their ends.
Because she had already lost consciousness and fallen.
Luna, confirming that the battle was over, swallowed the Litra cookie she was holding in one bite. Then, she approached the fallen Syris and said,
"Now, let's go back for treatment and head to the next battlefield, Labyrinth Master. We have no time to rest, no time."
